title: Steadfast Ops and Resilience Symposium

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-02 17:00 UTC | Duration: 72 minutes | Attendees: Ethan, Marina, Jordan, Priya, Sam, Ana, Devon, Rina, Tomas, Lina + company all-hands

Summary: leadership update then deep dive on resilience and ops zero to one. We go a little long on Q&A.

[00:00] Ethan Black (CEO): All right hello everyone, thanks for joining the resilience symposium, it's a little different than our typical all-hands but wanted a focused space on ops lessons and the SLO changes. Quick housekeeping: recording is on, please put questions in chat or raise hand.

[00:28] Marina Ortiz (CTO): Quick context, we'll do a brief post-mortem recap, then Priya will walk through the roadmap and the guardrails we're enabling, then Jordan and Sam will talk about Dedicated vs Hosted guidance, and we'll end with Q&A.

[01:05] Priya Nair (Head of Reliability): Hi all. So last quarter we had the cross-region degradation on Feb 11, it was an interplay between a model rollout, autoscaler mis-config, and a cache invalidation bug. I want to be very specific: this was not a single root cause, it was a cascade. We'll share the full timeline but main customer impact was higher latency and partial errors for a 45-minute window.

[01:46] Priya Nair: The key learnings — we need stronger rollout canaries for model variants, circuit-breakers for fallback routing, and more aggressive KPIs on cache eviction monitoring. We're proposing three immediate changes: 1) mandatory canary with 1% traffic for 24h for model rollouts > minor version, 2) autoscaler safety net thresholds and manual overrides, 3) KV cache eviction early-warning alerts.

[02:30] Ana Ruiz (Staff SRE): follow-up, the eviction metric wasn't firing because our threshold math was tuned to avg rather than p99; so it smoothed out the spike. we fix to p95/p99 and create synthetic workloads to trigger.

[03:05] Jordan Lee (VP Eng): On the autoscaler we found an interaction between burst scaling and GPU warm-up that led to token queueing. We're adding a warm-up policy and a staging pool for new model kernels. That should reduce cold-start hold times.

[03:42] (brief cross-talk) Devon Park: sorry — are we shipping on the kernel-staging this sprint?

[03:46] Jordan Lee: yes, the initial patches land this week, but full rollout will be staged.

[04:10] Sam Carter (Director, Product): From product: we'll formalize Dedicated vs Hosted decision tree. For customers with predictable throughput and strict data residency they'll still recommend Dedicated; for most developers the Hosted path with our new guardrails will be simpler and cheaper. We are publishing a one-pager for AE/SE.

[04:45] Ethan Black: A note on cost: the Optimize tool suggestions will be surfaced by default in Console so teams can see batching and quantization proposals. That should help customers reduce unit cost without manual tuning.

[05:10] Rina Shah (Head of Security): On the security front: SOC2 readiness is ongoing, we've completed control mapping for the incident and added additional audit logging for model rollouts. KMS tests for Private deployments are in progress; we will share spec and integration timelines.

[05:38] Tomas Green (Data Ops): quick ops note — the routing fallback was functional but slow; we need faster reroute when capacity tiers are unavailable. We'll tighten the policy to attempt local variant then remote region then degrade to gen-lite model within 8s.

[06:10] (Audience question in chat) Anonymous: can you clarify what 'gen-lite' means?

[06:18] Marina Ortiz: gen-lite is our shorthand for the lower-capacity model family that trades off some fidelity for latency and cost predictability. Not product name, just internal shorthand.

[06:40] Priya Nair: Ok real quick — proposed SLO changes. We are moving to a two-tier SLO for hosted: p95 latency 250ms, p99 latency 700ms with error budget burn alert at 2% per day. Dedicated customers can still negotiate bespoke SLOs. This is aimed to make our incident detection earlier.

[07:15] Jordan Lee: We will also expose more granular tracing in Console so token-level latency hotspots can be seen by route and model. expect a beta in 6 weeks.

[07:42] Ethan Black: Hiring and on-call changes — we're increasing SRE headcount by 3 in Q2, creating a rotational 'inference ops' pool and changing primary on-call to a 7-day shift to reduce context switching. People team will coordinate.

[08:05] Lina Gomez (People): we'll share rotation details and compensation adjustments. Also open office hours for anyone to flag concerns.

[08:28] (long pause / laughter)

[08:35] Q&A segment begins.

[08:38] Audience - Casey (Product): For Dedicated customers, what's the drift policy for pinned model versions? We had a customer ask about transparent patching.

[08:50] Sam Carter: pinned = pinned; we will not auto-upgrade pinned versions without explicit approval except for critical security patches after notice and a rollback window. We'll provide a patch window schedule.

[09:10] Audience - Dev (AE): When you say will publish Dedicated one-pager, will that include pricing guardrails?

[09:18] Ethan Black: pricing guardrails will be in a companion doc but not the full contract terms, more a guideline for AEs. Sam will lead.

[09:30] Audience - Morgan (Engineering): on KMS and Private — is the plan to support external HSMs? we have a regulator that needs HSM-backed keys.

[09:41] Rina Shah: yes, architecture supports external HSM integration via standard interfaces; we're validating through a partner POC. we'll publish the compliance checklist and a matrix of supported providers.

[10:03] Audience - Taylor (Research): will the gen-lite fallback degrade quality for hallucination-sensitive workloads?

[10:12] Priya Nair: yes, some quality trade-offs exist. for critical pipelines we'll recommend Dedicated with model pinning or enable a fallback that uses reranking with an embedding-based verifier. it's part of the risk playbook.

[10:35] (noise: someone typing)

[10:40] Ethan Black: ok last section — operational demos. Ana, can you briefly show the new alert dashboard?

[10:48] Ana Ruiz: yeah quick share — (screen noise) ok here's the eviction early-warning, it's a small micro dashboard that shows p95 cache fill rate, eviction spikes, and a synthetic traffic lane. We have thresholds highlighted and a runbook link.

[11:20] Ana Ruiz: note: the synthetic lane is not enabled by default in Hosted; it's opt-in for now. We'll evaluate auto enable after a few customer pilots.

[11:45] Jordan Lee: small engineering note — kernel staging pool will require model packaging changes, we will provide a converter tool. SEs, expect a slide deck and migration steps.

[12:05] Sam Carter: and sales — we'll do a brown-bag next week for AE/SE focused on resilience messaging and Dedicated decision guide.

[12:20] (Audience applause emoji in chat)

[12:25] Final recap by Ethan.

[12:28] Ethan Black: Recap: Priya publishes incident TL;DR, SRE runs tabletop, Product updates Dedicated docs, Security shares KMS spec. We will follow up in the engineering-all mailing list and schedule the AE brown-bag. Thanks everyone.

[12:50] (end recording)

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions had trouble with kernel-staging and some proper nouns; manual corrections applied where obvious.
